entries.description: Choosing, registering and configuring decision models for the anofox_decide DuckDB extension, and fixing setup errors. Covers every provider: stub, typesafe (TypeSafe Jev), liquid (Liquid AI D1), cloudflare (Clef, Clef-flash), openai (OpenAI Decisions gpt-6-luna), gemini (Gemini Decisions gemini-decision-1), systemone (Kev or any System One server), strands (strands-decider), and local (Julia-1, Laya). Covers the anofox_decide_allow_remote opt-in, the anofox_decide_model default, API keys as DuckDB secrets (CREATE SECRET TYPE anofox_decide, SERVICE ...) or env vars and their precedence, decide_services, decide_models, decide_doctor, every anofox_decide_* setting, the error-message shape and the common errors with their fixes, and installing / loading the extension (INSTALL anofox_decide FROM community). Use when setting up a model or a key, picking a provider, comparing hosted vs local, or when a decide_* call fails with "no model selected", "not registered", "remote calls are off", "no API key" or an HTTP error.

entries.name: anofox-decide-questions
entries.title: Anofox Decide — Questions & Decision Functions
entries.description: Asking natural-language questions about text or structured rows in SQL with the anofox_decide DuckDB extension. Covers the three question kinds (binary, choice, score) and every decision function: decide_probability (P(statement holds)), decide_decision (true/false at an explicit threshold), decide_choice and decide_choice_distribution (the best of options you define, and the probability of each), decide_score (the expected 0-based level on an ordered rubric), and several questions per text with decide_table (one row per question), decide_answers (the same rows as a LIST(STRUCT), unnested for whole tables) and decide_many (JSON). Also covers the questions JSON format, the decide_table output columns, NULLs and refusals, the model := argument and the anofox_decide_model default, structured state via to_json, installing and loading the extension, and the cheapest way to score a whole table (one decide_answers request per distinct text, joined back). Use when writing decide_probability / decide_decision / decide_choice / decide_choice_distribution / decide_score / decide_table / decide_answers / decide_many calls: classifying tickets, routing, flagging, rating, or tagging rows with an LLM decision model in SQL.
